title: Objective-oriented quantitative investment: A specification-driven framework for automated synthesis of trading strategy pipelines

p.t: Two decades of automation have transformed how trading strategies are built. Combined algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization (CASH) searches over preprocessing-and-model pipelines (Thornton et al., 2013;Feurer et al., 2015;Olson et al., 2016); neural architecture search (NAS) explores discrete spaces of predictor structures (Liu et al., 2019;Pham et al., 2018;White et al., 2023); evolutionary and reinforcement-learning systems mine formulaic alphas (Zhang et al., 2020;Yu et al., 2023); and, most recently, LLM-agent frameworks close the loop of hypothesis generation, implementation, and backtest feedback (Li et al., 2025;Wang et al., 2023;Novikov et al., 2025). Across this entire landscape, one element has remained constant: the objective is a scalar.

p.s: Validation loss, information coefficient, information ratio, Sharpe ratio-systems differ in what they search but not in what they seek.
p.t: This constancy is, on reflection, strange, because it is not how professional capital is allocated. A pension fund does not mandate "maximize Sharpe"; a quantitatively minded principal does not instruct a researcher to "maximize IC." Practitioners issue identity constraints: the return stream must be attributable to stock selection rather than to market direction or style timing; exposure to dividend and size factors must be zero; the strategy must remain profitable in unilateral declines; turnover must respect a cost budget; capacity must respect market impact. The celebrated decomposition of active returns into factor exposure and residual selection (Sharpe, 1992;Ang et al., 2009;Clarke et al., 2017) exists precisely because sophisticated capital refuses to pay for disguised beta. What is ordered is not a result but an objective profile; what is delivered must satisfy a specification, not merely win a leaderboard. We call the incumbent paradigm result-oriented: strategy construction is cast as d * = arg max d∈D g(θ(d)), where D is a space of candidate strategies, θ(d) a vector of evaluation statistics, and g a scalarization-typically one coordinate of θ. We propose Objective-Oriented Quantitative Investment (OOQI), in which the primitive object is a specification S-a structured collection of measurable, falsifiable clauses over θ-and the synthesis problem is to find assemblies that satisfy S, optimizing a scalar score only within the satisfying set:

The two paradigms are not merely different in emphasis; we show formally ( §3) and demonstrate empirically ( §7) that they select different strategies: result-oriented search systematically harvests whatever earns the score-including style beta-while specification-driven search purchases identity compliance at a measurable score cost. Why now: the LLM compiler. Specification-driven synthesis requires mapping semantic clauses ("zero style exposure") onto structural decisions (label neutralization, exposure-projection postprocessing, attribution clauses in evaluation). Until recently this mapping demanded a senior researcher. Large language models change the economics of the compiler: they carry the literature priors that turn blind combinatorial search into informed proposal-and-verification (Romera-Paredes et al., 2023;Novikov et al., 2025;Li et al., 2025). OOQI is deliberately agnostic about whether the compiler is an LLM agent, a Bayesian optimizer, or a human committee-but we note that LLM agents make the framework practical today.

1. A problem reframing with formal teeth ( §3). We define the strategy-pipeline design space with typed interface contracts, the strategy profile specification language with hard/soft clauses and priorities, and the satisfaction semantics d |= S. Three propositions establish: style contamination of result-oriented selection (P1); the non-negative, transfer-coefficient-like cost of specification (P2); and satisfaction inflation under search width, motivating deflated reporting (P3). 2. A specification language for strategy identity ( §5, App. B). Eight requirement families-signal quality, return-risk, purity/style, regime robustness, execution feasibility, portfolio structure, temporal behavior, transparency/compliance-comprising 30+ composable clauses, each with a measurement protocol grounded in an established literature prototype, plus an interaction algebra (synergy/conflict) and an arbitration semantics for conflicting objectives (App. C). 3. A verification protocol that treats satisfaction as a statistic ( §6, App. E). Search ledger accounting, temporal holdout isolated from search, random-assembly null models, multi-seed confidence intervals, and a deflated satisfaction rate adapting PBO/CSCV and Deflated-Sharpe corrections (Bailey et al., 2017;Bailey & López de Prado, 2014;Harvey et al., 2016) from single-metric selection bias to multi-clause specification satisfaction. 4. An illustrative demonstration ( §7, App. F). On a fully disclosed synthetic market with 32 pipeline assemblies, result-oriented selection attains the highest in-sample IR (7.10) while satisfying 25% of the specification; specification-driven selection satisfies 100% of it at 5.5% IR cost, and held-out satisfaction reveals the stochasticity that motivates our protocol. 5. An inverse-problem formalization ( §3.4, App. O). We identify specification-driven synthesis with the inverse problem of strategy synthesis, import Hadamard's well-posedness triad (existence/uniqueness/stability) as feasibility/underspecification/satisfaction-stability, and give margin-regularized selection a Tikhonov interpretation with a stability guarantee. 6. A theory of optimal assembly ( §4, App. D, O). We establish NP-hardness of satisfactiondriven assembly via a 3-SAT reduction (P4); a constant-factor approximation regime under conflict-free (coverage/submodular) composition (P5); quality measures for the satisfying setmargin profiles, certified radius, Pareto fronts, robust stress depth, and a quality-diversity archive reading; a Galois-connection duality between specifications and assemblies that yields identity inference and zero-cost clause completion (P6); Lagrangian shadow prices per clause (P7); and anytime-valid rolling certification via e-processes (P8). 7. A framework walkthrough and a real-complexity case study ( §8, §9). We fix the locus of each object-which decisions live in the design space, which in the specification, which in the protocol-on a production-shaped pipeline, state the locus of accountability that distinguishes objective-oriented selection from result-chasing, and decompose a documented macro-mesomicro coupling architecture into the framework's grammar: every architectural decision becomes a switch, every engineering red line finds its formal home (legality, clause, or protocol), and an interpretability clause grown from practice (w t ≥ 0.70) enters the transparency family.

Two gates against overfitting. The discipline proposed here operates through two sequential gates, neither of which is itself a test statistic. The first is architectural transparency: a strategy is not a monolithic model but an assembly over a contracted design space (Def. 1), in which every module declares a side-effect signature. One knows what one is building: each switch's effect on each evaluation coordinate is declared ex ante (the contract's side-effect signature) and measurable ex post. The two disciplines are complementary, and the measurement half is concrete: averaging the sixteen matched assembly pairs of the demonstration ledger that differ only in portfolio width, narrowing 50→20 raises mean |β| max by 7.12 (unstandardized DGP units, §7 footnote) and lowers mean IR by 1.39-the signature says which dials a switch moves; the ledger says by how much. Transparency is what makes the declared search width N computable-the nominal count of legal assemblies-and without a declared N the deflated statistics of §6 lack their essential input. The declared N does not exhaust the effective trials: threshold deliberation, discarded specification drafts, module authors' tacit choices, and fixed environment or context configurations ( §9) sit outside any architecture contract, and we flag them as residual channels rather than claim they are closed. The second gate is demand-side priority: the specification-what return, what risk, obtained through which declared exposures-is written down as clauses before any ledger is consulted. This blocks the psychology of overfitting at its root: the canonical single-shot HARKing mechanism-hypothesizing after the results are known (Kerr, 1998)-is structurally blocked when the target is registered before the arrow is shot, while residual channels (specification-shopping, informed threshold deliberation, repeated registration) are governed, not eliminated, by the disciplines of App. AE. The two gates compose into a mechanism: transparency makes N computable, giving deflated statistics their input; priority makes violations definable, turning overfitting from an invisible statistical drift into a detectable clause breach; the certificate and audit trail ( §6) make both attributable. The paradigm does not fight overfitting with cleverer models, but with the discipline of declare-compile-certify-audit.

Scope and honesty. OOQI is not a promise that any specification can be met: feasibility is decided by data, market, and budget, and the framework's duty is to report satisfaction or its absence with statistical integrity, never to manufacture it. The demonstration of §7 is synthetic by design-it validates the decision logic of the paradigm, not a live track record; a production case study is part of the research roadmap (App. H).

We organize four literature streams; an extended treatment is deferred to App. G. Table 1 summarizes the positioning. Supply-side automation: pipeline and architecture search. CASH formalizes joint algorithm selection and hyperparameter optimization over two-layer pipelines (Thornton et al., 2013); autosklearn adds meta-learning and ensembling (Feurer et al., 2015); TPOT evolves operator trees and is notable for a rare second objective (pipeline complexity) (Olson et al., 2016); CASH+ acknowledges that modern adaptation stages induce mutually incompatible search spaces (Balef et al., 2025). NAS searches discrete predictor structures (Liu et al., 2019;Pham et al., 2018); a meta-analysis of 1000 papers confirms that NAS targets accuracy, occasionally augmented by hardware-aware proxies (White et al., 2023). In finance, Qlib provides full-chain modularity without search (Yang et al., 2020a); Quant 4.0 articulates full-chain automation as a vision without formalization (Guo et al., 2024); evolutionary and RL systems search one stage-factor mining-with scalar fitness (Zhang et al., 2020;Yu et al., 2023). Modularity and combinatorial search have never met inside one quantitative system, and-with the exceptions we now acknowledge-search objectives remain scalars. Two neighboring literatures constrain search rather than merely optimize scalars, and we position against them honestly. Constrained Bayesian optimization (Gelbart et al., 2014;Hernández-Lobato et al., 2016) and safe reinforcement learning (Achiam et al., 2017) maximize objectives subject to probabilistic or expected-cost constraints; multi-objective and hardware-aware NAS (Tan et al., 2019;Lu et al., 2019) return Pareto fronts over accuracy and deployment proxies. These are the closest formal ancestors of our constrained selection, and §7 and App. F therefore include explicit baselines (penalty scalarization; Pareto filtering). Three deltas remain: constraints there are (i) probabilisticin-expectation rather than clause-wise auditable, (ii) defined over continuous knobs rather than typed pipeline identity, and (iii) unaccompanied by search-width deflation statistics. Specification formalisms from temporal logic (STL/MTL) offer hard/soft semantics we adopt, without strategyspace instantiation.

LLM-agent quantitative R&D. R&D-Agent evolves hypotheses under benchmark feedback and its quantitative instantiation jointly optimizes factors and models against IC/return metrics (Yang et al., 2025;Li et al., 2025). Alpha-GPT compiles natural-language trading ideas into formulaic alphas with human-in-the-loop review (Wang et al., 2023;Yuan et al., 2024). FunSearch and AlphaEvolve establish the LLM+evaluator+evolution paradigm against programmatically computable scalar evaluators (Romera-Paredes et al., 2023;Novikov et al., 2025). Decision-type agents trade directly rather than synthesize research (Zhang et al., 2024;Xiao et al., 2024). The closest specificationflavored precedent is an option-strategy DSL compiling intent into executable option structures (Luo et al., 2026); its requirement space (option legs, Greeks) shares nothing with strategy identity profiles, and it lacks satisfaction statistics. Existing systems start from data, metrics, or ideas; none starts from a verifiable multi-dimensional specification. Demand-side formalization. Goals-based wealth management replaces the scalar with targetachievement probability (Das et al., 2018;Deguest et al., 2015;Kim et al., 2020); institutional mandates formalize tracking-error and beta constraints (Roll, 1992;Jorion, 2003); the transfer coefficient prices the alpha destroyed by constraints (Clarke et al., 2002); pure-factor portfolios solve "exposure one to X, zero to all else" (Clarke et al., 2017); returns-based style analysis provides the canonical identity measurement (Sharpe, 1992); the Norwegian-commission evaluation established that apparent alpha is largely compensated factor exposure (Ang et al., 2009); regime models make market state a decision variable (Ang & Bekaert, 2002;Shu et al., 2024); multi-objective evolutionary methods trace Pareto fronts (Deb et al., 2002;Anagnostopoulos & Mamanis, 2009). Every clause of our language has an isolated mathematical prototype; no work unifies them into a composable specification language driving synthesis.

Evaluation credibility. Backtest overfitting is quantified by PBO/CSCV (Bailey et al., 2017); the Deflated Sharpe Ratio corrects selection bias, non-normality, and trial counts (Bailey & López de Prado, 2014); factor-zoo multiple testing demands thresholds rising with test counts (Harvey et al., 2016;Harvey & Liu, 2015); reality-check and SPA tests control data snooping pool-wide Table 1: Positioning: what starts the process, what is searched, what is sought. 3 Problem Formulation 3.1 The design space: modules with typed contracts Definition 1 (Module and assembly space). A strategy pipeline comprises K stages (in our reference instantiation, K=9: universe/data, label, feature processing, feature selection, predictor, training regime, post-processing, portfolio construction, risk overlay; App. A). Stage i offers a finite set M i of modules. Each module m ∈ M i declares (i) an input contract ι(m) and output contract o(m) over typed channels (panel shape, frequency, exposure structure, weight continuity); and (ii) a side-effect signature σ(m) ∈ R ds describing its first-order effect channels on evaluation coordinates (e.g., turnover pressure, exposure leakage, capacity footprint). An assembly d = (m 1 , . . . , m K ) is legal if contracts chain compatibly; the design space is With the module counts of App. A, |D| ≈ 4.4 × 10 7 at the module-family level and ≈ 8.8 × 10 8 once the families' discrete hyperparameter variants are counted (App. AI gives the two-level factorization). Three properties preclude exhaustive enumeration and motivate compilation: evaluation cost is minutes-to-hours per assembly; legality constraints couple stages (e.g., an exposure-projection postprocessor requires a predictor whose scores admit exposure regression); and stage effects interact non-additively (rank labels compound rank preprocessing; warm-start chaining offsets recency weighting). Definition 2 (Evaluation functional). Fix data and a backtest protocol. Evaluation maps an assembly to a statistics vector θ(d) ∈ R d θ whose coordinates include: information-coefficient family (RankIC mean, ICIR, positive-day share); return-risk coordinates (annualized excess, IR, max drawdown); identity coordinates (style exposure |β| max vs. a factor model, correlation with style indices, RBSA residual share); regime-conditional coordinates (conditional excess return and drawdown in downmarket states); feasibility coordinates (turnover, cost-sensitivity slope, capacity utilization); and structural coordinates (holdings count, industry deviation).

p.s: The specification: a language for strategy identity
p.t: Definition 3 (Specification). A strategy profile specification S = {c j } J j=1 is a set of clauses c j = (ϕ j , κ j , π j ) where: ϕ j : R d θ → {0, 1} is a measurable, falsifiable predicate over evaluation coordinates (a threshold predicate ϕ j (θ) = 1[θ j rel j τ j ] with rel j ∈ {≤, ≥}); κ j ∈ {HARD, SOFT} is the clause's force; and π j ∈ N is a priority. Write d |= c j iff ϕ j (θ(d)) = 1, and d |= S iff d |= c j for every HARD c j . The satisfaction rate is reported with the clause-wise vector ϕ j (θ(d)) j (the satisfaction profile). Clauses compose like building blocks; pairs interact as synergistic (joint satisfaction cheaper than separate), conflicting (joint satisfaction strictly costlier, up to infeasibility), or neutral (App. C formalizes via the cost functional below). Conflicts are arbitrated by a two-level semantics: HARD clauses carve the feasible set F(S); SOFT clauses enter a weighted objective or, under lexicographic priority, are satisfied in order π 1 ≻ π 2 ≻ • • • in the manner of goal programming (Kim et al., 2020).

Proofs are given in App. D. The propositions are elementary by design-their role is to make the paradigm's claims falsifiable and budgetable: contamination is not an accusation but a probability; cost is not a regret but a quantity with an upper bound; inflation is not a worry but an exponential law.

There is a classical mathematical duality that subsumes the two paradigms of Def. 4. Forward problems infer effects from causes: given an operator and its inputs, solve, and check whether the solution conforms to reality. Result-oriented research is the forward problem of quantitative financegiven assembly d and market realization ω, evaluate θ(d, ω) and inspect. Inverse problems infer causes from effects: given requirements on the solution, recover the operator. OOQI is exactly the inverse problem of strategy synthesis-given a specification on the return stream's identity, recover assemblies whose evaluation conforms. Inverse problem theory then organizes, under one roof, questions this paper has been asking all along (full formalization in App. O): Hadamard's triad-existence, uniqueness, stability-maps respectively onto feasibility of the specification (is F(S) empty?), underspecification (the satisfying set is typically an equivalence class, not a point), and stability of satisfaction (Proposition 3 is precisely an instability law); and Tikhonov-style regularization corresponds to our margin-maximizing selection and priority structure, which purchase stability at the price of bias. The market's operator being stochastic and nonstationary, the correct theoretical home is statistical inverse problems (Kaipio & Somersalo, 2005), and rolling re-certification is mandatory. We stress that the analogy is structural, and where it ends (App. O), it ends honestly.

p.s: Optimal Assembly: How to Compose, How to Judge, What Each Clause Costs
p.t: Definition 4 poses the synthesis problem; this section develops its theory. Three questions a principal inevitably asks next organize the development: how hard is optimal assembly ( §4.1); which member of the satisfying set should be returned, and how should the many tied solutions be judged ( §4.2, §4.3); and what does each clause cost in equilibrium ( §4.4). A statistical consequence for certification over time closes the section ( §4.5). Proofs are collected in App. D.

p.s: Composition is combinatorially hard-but not uniformly
p.t: The design space (Def. 1) motivates proposal-and-verification because exhaustion is infeasible. We now show the difficulty is intrinsic, not merely practical-and then isolate the structural regime in which principled approximation exists. Proposition 4 (NP-hardness of satisfaction-driven assembly). Deciding whether F(S) ̸ = ∅ is NPhard in the joint (stages × clauses) dimension, even when contract legality is trivial (all module pairs compatible) and every clause predicate is evaluable in polynomial time. With polynomial-time predicates, the problem is NP-complete. The reduction (App. D) is from 3-SAT: stages play the role of variables (two modules each), and each specification clause is satisfied iff the assembly contains at least one designated literal module; a fully satisfying assembly exists iff the formula is satisfiable. Two readings matter for practice. First, the source of hardness is interaction, not size: if every clause's satisfaction decomposes over single stages, feasibility is decidable in i |M i | by per-stage filtering-hardness enters exactly when clauses couple stages, the formal version of the observation in §3 that "legality constraints couple stages." Second, the compiler's proposer is thereby a heuristic oracle whose outputs must be certified rather than trusted: OOQI needs soundness only from the verifier, never from the proposer-the same asymmetry that underlies syntax-guided synthesis (Alur et al., 2013), where a specification, a grammar (here: typed contracts), and an untrusted synthesizer meet. Proposition 5 (A constant-factor regime under conflict-free composition). Suppose soft-clause satisfaction is coverage-structured: each clause c j designates a module family A j ⊆ i M i and is satisfied iff the assembly's module set meets A j , with clause weights w j ≥ 0. Then the weighted satisfaction f (d) = j w j ϕ j (d) is a monotone submodular function of the module set, and, under the one-module-per-stage (partition matroid) constraint, (i) a stage-wise greedy pass attains at least 1/2 of the optimum (Nemhauser et al., 1978), and (ii) the multilinear relaxation with pipage rounding attains at least 1 -1/e ≈ 0.63 (Calinescu et al., 2011). Conflicting clause pairs (App. C) break submodularity; characterizing approximation under supermodular conflict is open (roadmap R5).

p.s: Composition is combinatorially hard-but not uniformly
p.t: The practical content is a license and a warning. The license: when mechanisms compose without conflict, the compiler's greedy translation-assembly loop is not ad hoc but carries a constant-factor guarantee-certification then audits a search that was already principled. The warning: where conflicts dominate (the IC ⊖ turnover pair of Table 10 being the canonical instance), no such promise exists, and the certificate's deflation machinery is the only honest output. The theory thus tells the compiler when it may be fast and when it must be humble.

p.s: Many solutions: quality measures for the satisfying set
p.t: Remark 5 (App. O) records that F(S) is an equivalence class, not a point. Selection within the class requires quality measures. We define three at the level of an assembly and one at the level of the set; all are computable from quantities the compiler already produces. Definition 5 (Margin profile and certified radius). For assembly d and clause c j , let m j (d) be the signed distance of θj (d) inside the feasible half-space (App. O). The margin profile is the vector m(d) = (m j (d)) j ; the certified radius ρ(d) = min j m j (d)/s j normalizes by estimation scale: by Proposition 9, d retains full satisfaction under any evaluation perturbation with |ε j | < m j (d) in every coordinate. Bare satisfaction is a coin flip; deep satisfaction is a property. Definition 6 (Pareto-optimal assembly). weakly dominates it in score and in every hard-clause margin with at least one strict improvement. The certificate should return a Pareto front, not a point: the principal's risk appetite selects along it, and assemblies that tie in-sample are separated exactly by their margins-the stress-certification logic of (D'Amour et al., 2022) internalized into the solution concept. Definition 7 (Robust satisfaction and stress depth). Let the evaluation vary over an uncertainty set U of regime perturbations (drift shifts, volatility scaling, cost multipliers-the stress suite of App. E). The robustly satisfying set is F U (S) = {d ∈ D : F (d, ω) ∈ T for all ω ∈ U }-the robust-optimization counterpart of satisfaction (Ben-Tal et al., 2009). F U is monotone decreasing in U; the largest perturbation level at which d survives is its stress depth, a per-clause scalar the certificate can quote next to each margin.

p.s: Many solutions: quality measures for the satisfying set
p.t: Set-level quality: the specification archive. When the deliverable is a menu rather than a single assembly, the satisfying set itself needs a quality measure. Borrowing quality-diversity (Pugh et al., 2016): take the side-effect signature σ(d) (Def. 1) as the behavior descriptor, partition signature space into mechanism niches, and retain the best-margin certified assembly per niche. The archive's coverage (number of certified niches) times its depth (margins) is the quality score of the satisfying set-and it has an economic reading: niche-diverse certified assemblies fail through different mechanisms (crowding, regime change, cost shocks), so a principal allocating across the archive diversifies mechanism risk, which return-stream correlation alone cannot see. The satisfying set, properly measured, is a portfolio.

p.s: The specification lattice and identity inference
p.t: Definition 8 (Strength order and the identity map). Order specifications by entailment: S 1 ⪯ S 2 iff F(S 2 ) ⊆ F (S 1 ) ("S 2 is stronger"); quotienting by semantic equivalence yields the specification lattice, with join given by clause union-F(S 1 ∪ S 2 ) = F(S 1 ) ∩ F(S 2 ) is the least upper bound of the pair. For X ⊆ D, define the identity I(X) as the strongest specification satisfied by every d ∈ X. Proposition 6 (Galois structure). (F, I) is an antitone Galois connection between the specification lattice and the assembly powerset (Cousot & Cousot, 1977): Consequences: (i) completion-S ⪯ I(F(S)): every specification entails additional clauses that all its satisfying assemblies meet for free, certifiable at zero marginal search cost; (ii) identity inference-I({d}) is the strategy's inferred identity: the compiler run in reverse answers "what is this strategy?" from its evaluation vector, the inverse of the inverse problem of §3.4; (iii) equivalencetwo specifications denote the same feasible set iff their completions coincide, making semantic equivalence decidable through satisfaction rather than syntax. Consequence (i) has immediate engineering value: after certifying S, the certifier may report the bonus clauses I(F(S)) \ S-identity the principal did not order but provably receives. Consequence (ii) formalizes what due diligence has always done informally: reading a return stream and naming what it is.

p.s: The price of a clause: Lagrangian shadow prices
p.t: The interaction algebra (App. C) measures conflict through finite CoS differences. Constrainedoptimization theory supplies the marginal, equilibrium version. Write the synthesis problem with hard clauses as constraints h j (d) = θ j (d) -τ j ≥ 0 (oriented so feasibility is non-negativity), and consider the smoothed/relaxed formulation with Lagrangian Proposition 7 (Shadow price of a clause). Under standard regularity (local uniqueness of the optimum; linear independence of binding-constraint gradients), the envelope theorem (Milgrom & Segal, 2002) applied to the value function gives the optimal dual variable is the marginal score price of tightening clause j. The vector (λ * j ) j is thus a clause-level transfer coefficient in the sense of (Clarke et al., 2002)-the price list of identity-estimable in practice from the compiler's search history by local re-solves of the certified optimum. Remark 1 (Conflict as cross-price). In the smooth relaxation, pairwise conflict (Def. 9) corresponds to positive cross-partials: tightening clause j raises the shadow price of a conflicting neighbor, This reading is local and regularity-dependent; in the discrete design space the compiler estimates it by sensitivity of the certified optimum rather than by duality. We state it as a remark, not a proposition, deliberately. Two interpretations close the loop with neighboring fields. Economic: certificates can quote not just CoS but the per-clause price list-which identity is expensive, and whose price a conflicting neighbor is driving up (Remark 1); budgeting identity becomes as routine as budgeting tracking error. AI-theoretic: the compiler loop is constrained optimization in the sense of constrained MDPs (Altman, 1999), and Proposition 3 is precisely Goodhart's law (Manheim & Garrabrant, 2019) formalized for satisfaction statistics-any satisfaction measure used as a search target without ledger accounting inflates, so the deflation protocol of §6 is the Goodhart-resistant counterpart. In the alignment vocabulary: result-oriented research optimizes a proxy; OOQI specifies the objective and polices the proxy-objective gap statistically.

Rolling re-certification (App. O) tests the same clauses repeatedly as new data arrive, and classical p-value machinery inflates under such continuous monitoring. The e-value literature (Ramdas et al., 2023;Howard et al., 2021) supplies the instrument built for exactly this regime. Proposition 8 (Anytime-valid clause certification). For hard clause c j , let {E (j) t } t≥0 be a nonnegative supermartingale under the null that clause j fails (an e-process; for example, a mixture likelihood ratio computed on weekly margin observations). Then, by Ville's inequality, under the null a certificate that affirms clause j when E (j) t crosses 1/α is valid at level α simultaneously over all future inspection times-continuous re-certification pays none of the multiplicity penalty that rolling p-based tests incur (Ramdas et al., 2023). The operational reading upgrades the certificate from a document to a process: each certified clause ships with its e-process; certification is alive while E (j) t ≥ 1/α and lapses when it falls below. Alpha decay-a coupling classical theory does not model (App. O)-thereby becomes certificate expiry, a first-class, budgetable event rather than a silent drift of the truth. Nonparametric confidence sequences for the margins themselves (Howard et al., 2021) give the complementary estimation statement. 5 The OOQI Framework OOQI comprises three layers (Fig. 1): a demand layer (the specification language of Def. 3), a supply layer (the design space of Def. 1), and a compiler mediating them. We describe the compiler's three stages, then the arbitration of conflicting objectives.

p.s: Compiler stage I: translation (from specification to stage constraints)
p.t: Each clause is compiled into (i) constraints on stage-module admissibility, (ii) structural obligations, and (iii) evaluation obligations. Examples: a style-purity clause prunes non-neutralizing label modules (stage 2), mandates an exposure-projection or residualization post-processor (stage 7), and registers an attribution regression in evaluation; a turnover-budget clause admits only smoothing/buffer postprocessors and aim-portfolio-style portfolio modules (Gârleanu & Pedersen, 2013); a down-market resilience clause obliges regime-aware risk overlays (Ang & Bekaert, 2002;Shu et al., 2024) and adds regime-conditional coordinates to θ. Translation is where domain knowledge enters: the clauseto-mechanism mapping is curated from the literature prototypes of §2 (App. B gives the full table), and an LLM agent operationalizes it by proposing, for each clause, the module set consistent with the prototype's mechanism.

p.s: Compiler stage II: assembly (constrained proposal and verification)
p.t: Exhaustion of |D| ≈ 8.8 × 10 8 is impossible; assembly is proposal-and-verification. A proposer-LLM agent, Bayesian optimizer over the contracted space, or hybrid-emits candidate assemblies that (a) satisfy legality (Def. 1) and (b) are predicted-feasible under the translated constraints. Each candidate is evaluated on the search split, its satisfaction profile computed, and failures attributed: side-effect signatures (Def. 1) localize the responsible stage (e.g., a turnover-clause failure with an unsmoothed post-processor indicts stage 7), and the attribution re-enters the proposal prior. This loop differs from scalar AutoML in exactly one structural respect: feedback is clause-indexed, not scalar-the system learns which dimension failed, not merely that the score fell.

The surviving assembly is re-evaluated on a temporally isolated holdout under the protocol of §6, and the framework emits a satisfaction certificate: the clause-wise profile ϕ j j , the satisfaction rate with deflation SR def , the search ledger (N evaluated, search budget, seeds), the cost of specification CoS, and per-clause confidence statements. A specification that cannot be met is reported as infeasiblewith-evidence-which clauses failed, at what magnitudes, and which relaxations the interaction algebra identifies as cheapest (App. C). Honest infeasibility is a first-class output, not a failure mode.

Requirements interact. Three mechanisms, in order of application: (i) feasibility first-HARD clauses define F(S); if F = ∅, the compiler returns the minimal-cost relaxation identified by the conflict graph; (ii) weighted soft optimization-soft clauses contribute to a composite objective with principalset weights; (iii) lexicographic fallback-where a principal declares priorities, clauses are satisfied in order, accepting zero improvement on lower priorities once higher ones bind (Kim et al., 2020;Deguest et al., 2015). The interaction algebra (App. C) records, per clause pair, whether synergy or conflict was observed empirically across the search-turning folk knowledge ("turnover limits cost IC") into measured structure.

p.s: A Verification Protocol for Specification Satisfaction
p.t: Proposition 3 implies that satisfaction claims from searched spaces are presumptively inflated. The protocol below treats SR as a statistical object. Full technical details, including the deflation estimator, appear in App. E. 1. Search ledger. Every evaluated assembly is logged: the effective trial count N is a first-class reported quantity, exactly as DSR requires n trials (Bailey & López de Prado, 2014) and multipletesting thresholds require test counts (Harvey et al., 2016). 2. Temporal isolation. A terminal holdout period is never touched by search (no proposal, no early stopping, no attribution feedback), answering the nested-resampling requirement for unbiased model-selection evaluation (Cawley & Talbot, 2010). 3. Random-assembly null. Following NAS evaluation best practice (Yang et al., 2020b; Sciuto et al., 2020), M uniformly random legal assemblies are evaluated: the compiler must beat the null not on score but on feasibility discovery-finding assemblies in F(S) at rates exceeding chance. 4. Deflated satisfaction. For each clause, IS satisfaction is corrected for the expected spurioussatisfaction maximum under the ledger N (a clause-wise analogue of the expected-max-Sharpe correction (Bailey & López de Prado, 2014)); the deflated rate SR def discounts clauses whose apparent satisfaction is within the null band. 5. Cross-validated PBO over specifications. Adapting CSCV (Bailey et al., 2017): within each symmetric split, assemblies are ranked by IS satisfaction; we compute the rank of the IS-optimal assembly's satisfaction in the OOS half and report the fraction of splits where this OOS rank falls below the median-the probability of satisfaction backtest overfitting-with PBO < 0.1 as deployability guidance (App. E). 6. Stress certification. Each clause ships with a stress test in the spirit of underspecification certification (D'Amour et al., 2022): purity clauses are re-examined under rotated factor premia; resilience clauses under synthetic unilateral-decline regimes; cost clauses across a cost-sensitivity curve rather than a point assumption (Novy-Marx & Velikov, 2016; Frazzini et al., 2018).

We demonstrate that the two paradigms of Def. 4 select different objects on a fully disclosed synthetic market (all parameters in App. F; single fixed seed, no tuning). N =300 stocks, T =208 weeks (156 IS / 52 held-out); returns load on market, size, and dividend-style factors plus a mild-momentum+quality idiosyncratic alpha; the style premium is positive in-sample and reverses held-out-a stylized style-rotation regime. The assembly space varies five binary stage choices (label horizon, signal neutralization, signal smoothing, portfolio width, turnover buffer): |D| = 32 legal pipelines. The pipeline as choice points. A strategy is not a monolithic object but a composition of choice points; each stage offers a small number of categories, and the design space is their legality-filtered product (Def. 1). Table 4 instantiates this on a production-shaped equity pipeline. The unification the framework claims is at the level of form-arg max d∈F (S) g(θ(d)) at every stage and every product thereof-while heterogeneity of objectives is absorbed into an explicitly declared S. A specification, declared before any ledger. The demand side enters as a clause table: each clause carries a threshold, a hard/soft type, and a one-line commercial rationale (Table 5). The discipline that makes this table evidentiary rather than decorative is priority: thresholds are taken from the institution's standing risk-governance documents and frozen-with a hash-before any ledger is consulted (the protocol's pre-registration step, App. E). Thresholds read off the ledger are HARKing (Kerr, 1998) with extra steps. The locus of accountability. Result-oriented selection, we argue, carries a structural accountability deficit: "it ranked first in the backtest" outsources judgment to a statistical artifact. Objective-oriented selection does not answer to results alone-its primitive is arg max d∈F (S) g(θ(d)), optimization within a contract-and it attaches accountability at three explicit points: (i) certified feasibility of the selected assembly against the declared S; (ii) an auditable selection trace-the compiled feasible set, the winner's margins, and the runner-up; (iii) post-deployment monitoring of each clause, with predefined remedies on violation. This is a relocation of responsibility, not its removal, and the relocation is conditional in a way we state plainly: certificates testify about ledgers, not about the future, and when the specification itself is badly written-thresholds politicized, clauses missingcompliance with it certifies the wrong thing well. Clause-level outcome accountability therefore attaches to two objects, not one: the assembly (did it satisfy S?) and the specification writer (was S the right contract?). The difference from certification-washing ( §10) is operational rather than rhetorical: a ranking is a single number with no stated terms of engagement, whereas a certificate enumerates what was promised, the margin on each promise, and the evidence retained-giving an evaluator something a leaderboard never provides, namely the list of commitments against which to hold the author.

p.s: Case Study: Decomposing a Macro-Meso-Micro Coupling Idea
p.t: The demonstration of §7 validates decision logic on five switches; this section exercises the framework on an idea of real complexity, contributed from practice under the same single-source, anonymized conditions disclosed in the ethics paragraph of §10: a fully documented macro-meso-micro threelevel coupling stock-selection architecture (dual-channel regime state center; an interpretable cascade engine multiplying micro scores by meso and macro coefficients; an end-to-end engine with forced interaction features and FiLM conditioning; dynamic gating between engines; four guardrails). The source document prescribes one fixed architecture chosen by argument among four candidates. The framework's move is to restore that point to its space: every architectural decision becomes a switch, every engineering red line finds a formal home, and the champion must re-win with a certificate. Acts 1-4 are completed here; acts 5-7 (compilation, adjudication, audit) are protocol-defined and marked [TBD], pending the same pre-registered exhibit pipeline as §8. Act 1: the idea, stated colloquially. "Couple the macro cycle, the meso industry layer, and micro stock selection into one system, so that the regime view disciplines the alpha and the market's own structure corrects the regime view." The sentence is admirably clear and operationally meaninglessexactly the raw material the framework exists for. Act 2: decomposition into the grammar. Applying the rule "which stage's behavior does this idea change?" maps the architecture onto the nine-stage grammar of App. A (Table 6). Three components exit the design space entirely: the data platform and the attribution layer are protocol and audit infrastructure, not modules; the regime state center is an environment service-an upstream context provider emitting (p t , D t , z t ) that clauses may reference but that no assembly contains. We are explicit about the cost of this choice: the end-to-end engine conditions on the state center's outputs, so assemblies identical in every switch but differing in environment configuration are behaviorally distinct yet indistinguishable in the registry; the environment configuration is therefore fixed ex ante, declared on the certificate, and kept outside the accounted search width, as a disclosed residual degree of freedom rather than a hidden one. What remains is a set of switches.

Two rows of Table 6 exceed the reference grammar of App. A, whose S7 inventory contains post-processing modules but no coefficient modulation or fusion. That appendix declares itself "a reference grammar, not a closed world"; this case exercises that clause. We extend S7 with a coefficient-modulation/fusion family (multiplicative regime coefficients; engine-blending gates), and we count an assembly carrying both end-to-end variants as a single ensemble module whose members are trained jointly-so the product structure of the design space and the counting convention for N are preserved, with each fusion-family variant counting as one S7 choice. The compiler-mapping anchor of C8.4 (App. I) refers to this extended family. Act 3: registration. The four candidate architectures the source document compares-pure cascade; pure end-to-end; static blend; dual-engine dynamic coupling-enter the registry as four named Act 4: contracting. The institution's demand side is declared as clauses before any ledger: the four standard hard clauses of Table 5 (thresholds anonymized, [TBD]) plus one clause this case contributes to the language: an interpretability clause w t ≥ 0.70, requiring the interpretable engine to retain at least 70% of the fused score at all times (we write w t for the gating weight here; ω is reserved for market realizations elsewhere). The source document states this as an engineering red line; the framework formalizes it as a clause. Its family membership deserves care: the predicate constrains the fusion structure rather than the return stream directly-a 70%-weighted interpretable engine does not by itself make 70% of the P&L interpretable-so the clause's nearest structural neighbor is F6 (portfolio/fusion structure)-though no F6 clause currently covers fusion, a cookbook gap we flag rather than patch silently-while its rationale belongs to F8; we register it in F8 as the new entry C8.4 (App. I). We claim no more than that it is a practitioner-grown instance of the transparency family-the clause cookbook itself being partly informed by the same single practitioner source disclosed in §10, the practice/cookbook boundary is porous, and we flag it rather than celebrate it. The remaining red lines of the source design find their formal homes (Table 7). One boundary case is instructive: orthogonalization both transforms a signal and disciplines its measurement, and the arbitration rule we adopt is that whatever changes the object is a module; whatever governs the evidence is protocol-the row is therefore split rather than forced into one home. Acts 5-7, protocol-defined and pending. Compilation (legality filtering under the long-panel contract; feasible-set compilation under the clause set), adjudication (arg max g within F(S), margin audit, certificate issuance under a pre-registered specification hash), and audit (the D t -dynamic range switch and the guardrail package measured as cost-benefit switches on the ledger) follow the protocol of §6 and the pre-registration discipline of §8. Two outcomes are equally informative: if the documented champion re-wins, its argument becomes evidence; if a sibling assembly wins, the framework has done its work once already. Until those data arrive, this section should be read as a protocol-defined walkthrough of a real architecture, not as empirical evidence. Anonymization: this section exposes architecture (stage map, switches, clause types) and nothing else-no signal definitions, parameters, or performance data; module identities follow the S1-S9 abstraction.

Is this a paradigm shift? In the structural sense, yes: the reframing changes what counts as a legitimate question-from which strategy scores highest to which assembly satisfies this identity-and supplies the three institutions a paradigm requires: a language (Def. 3), a machine (the compiler), and a court (the protocol). It is equally important to state what kind of shift it is not. It is not a new alpha source, not a claim that specifications will be met, and not a repudiation of the existing literature: every clause stands on an established prototype, and the compiler stands on the AutoML and LLM-agent advances it reframes. Paradigm shifts are ratified by adoption, not proclamation; we therefore state the falsifiable adoption criteria: (a) specifications reused across institutions (language externalizes value); (b) certificates accepted as evidence by evaluators (statistics carry trust); (c) measured CoS entering practitioner decisions (the cost of identity becomes a budgeted quantity, as the transfer coefficient did twenty years ago (Clarke et al., 2002)). Relation to the nearest neighbors. Alpha-GPT takes an idea-a directional hint about what might work; OOQI takes a specification-a verifiable constraint set about what must hold. R&D-Agent-Quant evolves hypotheses pulled by backtest numbers; OOQI constrains assemblies pushed by clauses. Declarative ML argues that users should state what they want in general machine learning (Molino & Ré, 2022); OOQI supplies the domain language, satisfaction statistics, and credibility protocol that make that argument actionable where the stakes-capital-demand them.

Limitations. (i) The clause inventory, though broad (App. B), cannot exhaust practitioner intent; the language must be extensible, and clause engineering is itself expertise. (ii) Satisfaction predicates over backtest statistics inherit every fragility of backtesting; our protocol mitigates but cannot abolish this. (iii) The compiler's proposal quality currently depends on LLM priors that may be shallow exactly where markets are subtle. (iv) The demonstration is synthetic; the research roadmap (App. H) includes a live-system re-architecture case study under anonymized conditions. Ethics, dual use, and conflicts. A framework that makes identity constraints explicit also makes their absence conspicuous; it does not eliminate the misuse of backtests, and its certificates must never be read as guarantees of future performance. Three risks deserve explicit treatment. (i) Certification-washing: the framework's own dual-use hazard is that a satisfaction certificate could lend a statistical veneer to overfit strategies-lowering epistemic standards while claiming to raise them. Our mitigations are structural: certificates carry deflation and retention intervals rather than binary verdicts, ledgers are hashable and auditable, and certificates expire with the evaluation window. (ii) Crowding and reflexivity: if many principals order the same identity (e.g., "pure selection alpha"), the alpha the certificates certify decays by the aggregate adoption; a certificate describes a strategy, not its crowd, and widespread adoption of any specification is itself a regime change the monitor must detect. (iii) Conflicts of interest: the clause inventory of App. B was informed by a qualitative diagnosis of a live production strategy operated by the author's employer (Shanghai Liangbai Technology Co., Ltd.); the diagnosis is used in anonymized form only, no production code, parameters, or performance data appear in this paper, and the planned production case study (roadmap R1) will be subject to the same constraint. Readers should treat the demand-layer grounding as single-source practitioner input-useful for concreteness, not a substitute for multi-institutional elicitation. Broader impact: if adopted, the framework shifts quant research disclosure from "results achieved" to "requirements met," which we believe benefits allocators, regulators, and end investors; its failure modes (bad forward operators, politicized thresholds) are discussed in §10.

We have argued that automated quantitative research has been solving the wrong problem, and we have built the alternative: a specification-driven framework-language, compiler, and statisticsin which investors order identities and systems deliver satisfaction certificates. The apparatus is deliberately conservative: every clause grounded in established measurement science, every claim deflated for search, every infeasibility reported honestly. If the field adopts even the modest habit of reporting which clauses a strategy satisfies alongside how high it scores, the reframing will have done its work.

Requirements compose like building blocks, and blocks push against or reinforce one another. This appendix formalizes pairwise interaction and the arbitration semantics used by the compiler ( §5).

p.s: C.1 Interaction via the cost functional
p.t: Recall Definition 9 (Pairwise interaction). For hard clauses c i , c j , define the incremental costs ∆ i = CoS({c i }), ∆ j = CoS({c j }), ∆ ij = CoS({c i , c j }). Monotonicity of CoS (Proposition 2) gives ∆ ij ≥ max(∆ i , ∆ j ), and the pair is an exhaustive partition with tolerance ε set by estimation noise. Synergy is the free-rider regime: satisfying the dearer clause buys the cheaper one. Conflict is super-additive cost: the pair costs more than the sum of its parts because the mechanisms that buy one clause (e.g., slow signals for turnover) destroy the other (e.g., fast signals for IC).

Given S with conflict graph (V, E ⊖ ): 1. Feasibility check: if the conflict graph contains a known-infeasible clique (e.g., {high IC, low turnover, tight horizon} beyond measured bounds), return the minimum-cost relaxation: the clause whose removal maximizes restored feasibility per unit of principal's priority loss. 2. Weighted soft mode: maximize g + j:κj =SOFT w j ϕ j over F(S hard ), weights set by the principal. 3. Lexicographic mode: satisfy soft clauses in priority order π 1 ≻ π 2 ≻ . . . , freezing each satisfied clause as hard before descending-the goal-programming semantics of (Kim et al., 2020) lifted from wealth targets to identity clauses.

This appendix expands §2 with per-work annotations; every entry was verified against arXiv/venue records in August 2026. G.1 Supply-side automation CASH lineage. Auto-WEKA (Thornton et al., 2013) first unified algorithm selection and hyperparameters in one hierarchical Bayesian-optimization problem; auto-sklearn (Feurer et al., 2015) added meta-learned warm starts and post-hoc ensembles (JMLR 2020/2022 v2); TPOT (Olson et al., 2016) evolves operator trees via genetic programming and is, to our knowledge, the only mainstream AutoML system with a built-in second objective (pipeline size); auto-PyTorch (Zimmer et al., 2021) fuses NAS with CASH; CASH+ (Balef et al., 2025) generalizes CASH to heterogeneous modern pipelines but explicitly retreats to a two-layer selection over incompatible spaces-an admission that interface contracts (our Def. 1) are the missing abstraction. NAS. DARTS (Liu et al., 2019) relaxes discrete cells to continuous mixtures; ENAS (Pham et al., 2018) shares parameters across subgraphs; the 1000-paper meta-analysis (White et al., 2023) confirms the field's objective is accuracy with occasional hardware-aware proxies, and its evaluation is fragile (Yang et al., 2020b;Sciuto et al., 2020). No NAS work accepts semantic specifications as input. Quant-side automation. Qlib (Yang et al., 2020a) modularizes the full chain (data, model, backtest, portfolio, execution) but assembles by human workflow files; Quant 4.0 (Guo et al., 2024) argues for end-to-end automation as a vision; AutoAlpha (Zhang et al., 2020) and AlphaGen (Yu et al., 2023) search the factor stage alone with scalar fitness, as do AlphaAgent (Tang et al., 2025) and AlphaForge. The modularity-search intersection inside one quantitative system remains unoccupied.

R&D-Agent (Yang et al., 2025) abstracts data-science R&D as hypothesis-implement-feedback evolution; its quantitative version (Li et al., 2025) co-evolves factors and models against IC/return feedback, reporting strong backtest results at sub-$10 research cost-the engineering nearest to our compiler, but with metrics, not specifications, as the steering signal. Alpha-GPT (Wang et al., 2023) and its successor (Yuan et al., 2024) compile natural-language trading ideas into alphas with human-inthe-loop review; we distinguish ideas (search-direction hints) from specifications (verifiable constraint sets) as disjoint input types. FunSearch (Romera-Paredes et al., 2023) and AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al., 2025) prove the LLM+evaluator+evolution loop against programmatically computable scalar evaluators; OOQI can be read as replacing their scalar evaluator with a specification satisfier-plus the statistics to trust it. Decision-type agents (Zhang et al., 2024;Xiao et al., 2024;Yang et al., 2024) execute trades or reports, orthogonal to synthesis. The option-strategy DSL (Luo et al., 2026) is the closest specification-shaped neighbor, differing in requirement space (option legs/Greeks vs. identity profiles) and lacking satisfaction statistics. Declarative ML (Molino & Ré, 2022) supplies the philosophical charter-separate what from how-which we instantiate for quantitative identity.

Goals-based wealth management (Das et al., 2018) replaces scalar risk with goal-achievement probability; (Deguest et al., 2015) layers goals by importance with risk budgets; (Kim et al., 2020) gives the lexicographic goal-programming machinery our arbitration reuses. Mandate constraints (Roll, 1992;Jorion, 2003) are the ancestors of F6 clauses; the transfer coefficient (Clarke et al., 2002) prices constraint cost and inspires Proposition 2. Pure-factor portfolios (Clarke et al., 2017) are the mathematical prototype of style-zero clauses; RBSA (Sharpe, 1992) and the Norwegian evaluation (Ang et al., 2009) supply the measurement and the evidentiary standard for alpha purity. Regime work (Ang & Bekaert, 2002;Shu et al., 2024) grounds F4; multi-objective evolutionary methods (Deb et al., 2002;Anagnostopoulos & Mamanis, 2009) supply Pareto machinery but flatten requirements into objective vectors, losing hard/soft semantics and priorities. Requirements engineering for ML (Vogelsang & Borg, 2019;Rahimi et al., 2019) contributes vocabulary (elicitation, specification, verification) without financial instantiation. G.4 Evaluation credibility PBO/CSCV (Bailey et al., 2017), DSR (Bailey & López de Prado, 2014), Haircut-Sharpe (Harvey & Liu, 2015), factor-zoo corrections (Harvey et al., 2016), reality check/SPA (White, 2000; Hansen, 2005), model-selection overfitting (Cawley & Talbot, 2010), NAS search-phase evaluation (Yang et al., 2020b; Sciuto et al., 2020), and underspecification certification (D'Amour et al., 2022). None combines multi-clause satisfaction with search-width deflation; that combination-spec satisfaction × search-level multiple testing-is, to our knowledge as of August 2026, unoccupied, and constitutes the protocol's claim to novelty.

p.s: J Formal Grammar of the Specification Language
p.t: The specification language is a small typed DSL. We give its concrete syntax in BNF, its typing rules, and its semantics. J.1 Concrete syntax spec := "spec" ident "{" { clause } "}" clause := "clause" ident ":" predicate [ "hard" | "soft" ] [ "priority" int ] [ "protocol" ident ] [ "family" familyid ] predicate := atom { ("and" | "or") atom } atom := coord rel thresh [ "window" range ] [ "state" stateid ] coord := "rankic_mean" 4. Contract reachability: each clause's compiler mapping must reach at least one stage whose module set is non-empty after prior pruning; otherwise the spec is statically infeasible and rejected before any backtest. 5. Priority well-foundedness: priorities form a total preorder; cycles in stated preferences are rejected.

The denotation of a spec is the pair (F(S), g S ): a feasible set and a scalarization. Hard clauses conjoin into F; soft clauses define g S = g + j w j ϕ j under weighted mode, or the lexicographic order under priority mode. Satisfaction d |= S and SR are as in Def. 3. Two specs are equivalent if they denote the same (F, g S ); the parser normalizes for equivalence checking (clause reordering, threshold algebra on identical coordinates).

p.s: L Robustness of the Demonstration Across Seeds
p.t: The main-text demonstration uses one disclosed seed. Here we repeat the full experiment on ten seeds (identical DGP and protocol, seed varying), reporting per-seed selections of both paradigms (Table 20). Findings. (i) Feasibility is itself random: the satisfying set contains 0 to 10 of 32 assemblies (mean 4.8 ± 3.1); seed 6 admits no feasible assembly-an organically occurring INFEASIBLE-WITH-EVIDENCE case, demonstrating that honest infeasibility reporting is not a corner case but a routine possibility. (ii) Result-oriented satisfaction is a coin flip: A's in-sample satisfaction averages 0.57 ± 0.37, spanning 0.00 to 1.00-sometimes the score leader happens to be pure, sometimes it violates every identity clause; the paradigm offers no control. (iii) Objective-oriented satisfaction is exact in-sample on every feasible seed (1.00 ± 0.00)-a definitional property of constrained selection, not an empirical finding, since d * F is selected inside F-and is directionally more stable held-out (0.72 ± 0.20 vs. A's 0.62 ± 0.32). We stress the honest statistics: the paired difference over the nine feasible seeds (mean +0.11, sd 0.22) is not significant (exact two-sided sign test, p = 0.375), and under the convention that an infeasible draw scores SR = 0, B's held-out mean is 0.65 rather than 0.72-we report both conventions. What constrained selection provably removes is in-sample satisfaction variance; the held-out variance reduction is a consistent tendency this sample cannot confirm. (iv) Cost of specification varies from 0 (spec and score agree) to 1.81 IR points (mean 0.53 ± 0.58), consistent with Proposition 2: cost is a quantity with a distribution, budgetable ex ante by the temptation bound. (v) Held-out style violations, when they occur, are comparable in magnitude across paradigms here-an honest null result that strengthens the case for clause-wise stress certification rather than paradigm triumphalism.

Even ten seeds of one DGP probe one corner of the space of markets; we present this as logic validation, and the real-data robustness study is roadmap R1/R2. We deliberately report all seeds including the inconvenient ones (0, 2, 8, where A is fully or mostly compliant, and 6, where nothing complies).

p.s: M Worked Implementation Case: A Neural Realization of a Pure-Alpha Specification
p.t: This appendix walks the compiler end-to-end on one specification, producing a concrete neural architecture-SpecNet-as the certified assembly. Two remarks frame the case. First, the predictor is deliberately not a gradient-boosted tree: the point of the exercise is that the specification, not modeling habit, selects the structure; a neural assembly with exposure-aware components satisfies clauses that tree assemblies satisfy only through external post-processing. Second, this is an engineering blueprint with a verification plan (per §6), not a claimed track record; the reference implementation accompanies this paper.

A principal states, in practitioner diction: "Pure cross-sectional stock-selection alpha; zero exposure to market direction, size, dividend and growth styles; uncorrelated with the dividend index; must not bleed in unilateral declines; profits realize early in the holding week; turnover within budget." Parsing (App. J) yields: spec PURE_ALPHA_WEEKLY { clause C31 : beta_abs(mkt) <= 0.05 and beta_abs(size) <= 0.05 and beta_abs(div) <= 0.05 and beta_abs(growth) <= 0.05 hard family F3 protocol EXPO_REG clause C32 : corr_abs(dividend_index) <= 0.10 hard family F3 protocol IDX_CORR clause C41 : cond_excess(down_quintile) >= 0.0 hard family F4 protocol STATE_COND clause C51 : tov <= 0.10 hard family F5 protocol TOV_ONeway clause C71 : profit_conc(5) >= 0.55 soft priority 1 family F7 protocol EVENT_STUDY clause C11 : rankic_mean >= ledger(0.02) soft priority 2 family F1 protocol IC_WEEKLY } M.2 Translation: from clause to mechanism Stage-I translation (Table 21) constrains: S2 to residual or hedged labels; S5 to predictors admitting exposure-aware training; S7 to smoothing+buffer; S9 to a regime-gated overlay. The residuallabel obligation and the turnover budget jointly rule out plain tree ensembles without external machinery (their scores carry raw style loadings and oscillate week to week); a neural predictor with an adversarial de-styling head and a differentiable turnover penalty satisfies both obligations inside the model-the compiler's stated reason for preferring it here. M.3 The assembled architecture SpecNet (Fig. 3): per-name feature sequences (20 weeks × F features, grouped into families: mild-momentum, quality, liquidity, volatility, sentiment) enter a family-gated temporal encoderper-family GRUs whose outputs are mixed by learned gates, letting the model express the "mild momentum + quality" tilt as gate marginals rather than fixed weights. A cross-sectional attention layer contextualizes each name against the week's universe (relational ranking in the spirit of (Feng et al., 2019)). The representation feeds two heads: a score head (listwise rank loss over the cross-section) and an adversarial style head that tries to predict the factor realizations from the score-gradient reversal forces the score representation to be unpredictive of style (Ganin et al., 2016), mechanizing feature sequences 20wk × F , 5 families family-gated temporal encoder (per-family GRU + gates)

cross-sectional attention score head Lrank adversarial style head (reversed) exposure projection + EMA + buffer + regime overlay C3.1/C3.2 inside training. Post-processing applies exposure projection, EMA smoothing (α = 0.4), and a buffer band (N +8); a regime overlay gates gross exposure by jump-model state probabilities (Shu et al., 2024). Training is rolling-window with warm-start chaining; the loss is with L style the adversary's (reversed) objective, tov a differentiable turnover surrogate, and L down weighted ranking loss on down-state weeks.

p.t: Certification follows §6: temporal holdout isolated from all architecture and hyperparameter decisions; search ledger counting every evaluated variant; clause-wise deflation; stress suite (factor-premium rotation, synthetic unilateral decline, cost grid). No performance claim is made here: this appendix demonstrates the compiler's output form-a complete, clause-traceable architecture-on a blueprint that is deliberately distinct from any GBDT-based production system. p.s: N.1 Five rules of good specifications
p.t: 1. Every hard clause must hurt to lose. If you would not walk away from a strategy that violates it, it is soft. Over-hardening is the top cause of static infeasibility. 2. Pin protocols, not just thresholds. "Low correlation" without a declared index, window, and estimator is a wish, not a clause (Popper rule, App. J). 3. Budget the interactions. Consult the conflict matrix (Table 10) before pairing IC-level demands with turnover budgets or purity with capacity. 4. Order your soft clauses. Unprioritized soft lists delegate arbitration to the optimizer's whims; lexicographic priority is cheaper to state than to regret. 5. Demand the certificate, not the story. A satisfying narrative without ledger N , deflation, and holdout isolation is marketing. N.2 Ten profiles, one language (the thousand-faces property)

p.s: O Inverse-Problem Formalization: Well-Posedness of Strategy Synthesis
p.t: This appendix develops the inverse-problem reading of §3.4 into the framework's fourth theoretical pillar. References for the classical theory: Hadamard's well-posedness doctrine (Hadamard, 1902), Tikhonov regularization (Tikhonov, 1963), the standard monograph on deterministic inverse problems (Engl et al., 1996), statistical inversion (Kaipio & Somersalo, 2005), and PDE-constrained optimization (Hinze et al., 2009).

p.s: O.1 The forward operator and the duality
p.t: Definition 10 (Forward operator). Let Ω be the space of market realizations (return panels and auxiliary data paths) and Θ ⊂ R d θ the statistics space (Def. 2). The forward operator F : D×Ω → Θ maps an assembly and a realization to evaluation statistics. Forward problem: fix d, sample ω, compute F (d, ω), verify against reality-this is backtesting. Inverse problem: given a target set T ⊆ Θ defined by specification predicates, find d such that F (d, ω) ∈ T with high probability over ω-this is OOQI synthesis. The duality is exact in one direction and statistical in the other: the forward map is well-defined (every assembly evaluates to statistics), while the inverse map is set-valued, noise-corrupted, and-as we now show-classically ill-posed in all three Hadamard senses, with each ill-posedness already tamed by a component of the framework.

Remark 4 (Existence characterization-partly conjectural). F(S) ̸ = ∅ iff T ∩ R ̸ = ∅, where R = conv{F (d, ω) : d ∈ D} is the reachable statistics set. Two useful consequences: (i) static infeasibility-if a clause's mechanism chain reaches no module after contract pruning (App. J, rule 4), then T ∩ R = ∅ is decidable before any backtest; (ii) mechanism reachability (conjecture)-if every clause admits a mechanism chain and the stage module sets are non-empty, then for thresholds in the interior of the reachable coordinate ranges, existence should hold except on a measure-zero boundary; we do not prove this genericity statement, and flag it as the formal gap a full proof requires; infeasibility then concentrates on threshold ambition (too-tight τ ) and conflicting joints (App. C), which is exactly what the certifier's relaxation report quantifies. The ten-seed study (App. L) instantiates both cases: nine seeds are feasible (existence holds, uniqueness fails), seed 6 is infeasible (existence fails)-and the framework's duty in that case is precisely the inverse-problem duty: report non-existence with evidence rather than force a fit. O.3 Uniqueness: the satisfying set is an equivalence class Remark 5 (Non-uniqueness / underspecification). Whenever clauses constrain k < d θ coordinates and F(S) ̸ = ∅, the satisfying set F(S) is generically not a singleton: any two assemblies differing only in unconstrained coordinates both satisfy. Hence inverse solutions form an equivalence class [d], and additional distinguishing functionals are required to select within the class.

This is the inverse-problem restatement of the underspecification doctrine (D'Amour et al., 2022): stress tests are exactly the distinguishing functionals-they separate class members that tie in-sample. The compiler's stress suite (App. E) is therefore not an extra precaution but the theoretically mandated completion of the solution concept.

p.s: O.4 Stability: margins as Tikhonov regularization
p.t: Clause predicates are evaluated on noisy estimates: θj (d) = θ j (d) + ε j , |ε j | ≤ δ j w.h.p. Naive selection on φ is unstable (Proposition 3). Define the margin of assembly d on clause c j as m j (d) = signed distance of θj (d) inside the feasible half-space, and the margin-regularized selection Proposition 9 (Stability via margins). If d λ is selected with worst hard-clause margin m min (d λ ) ≥ max j δ j , then satisfaction of all hard clauses is retained under perturbations up to max j δ j : the estimate's satisfaction is stable to the noise level. Conversely, any selection with m min < max j δ j admits a noise realization within bounds that flips a hard clause. Margin maximization is thus exactly Tikhonov regularization for the inverse problem-stability purchased with bias (score sacrificed to CoS, Proposition 2). The proof is one line: m j (d) ≥ δ j implies θ j (d) stays in the feasible half-space for any |ε j | ≤ δ j . Its content is practical: certificates should report margins, and selection should prefer assemblies that satisfy clauses deeply, not barely-the inverse-problem justification for the deflation margin s j √ 2 log N of App. E.

p.s: O.5 Bayesian reading and the adjoint link
p.t: Two further correspondences complete the picture. Bayesian inversion (Kaipio & Somersalo, 2005): a prior π(d) over assemblies (the LLM prior over mechanisms, App. K), a likelihood from evaluation evidence ( θ given d), and a posterior over D whose credible sets answer "which assemblies plausibly satisfy S"-the satisfaction certificate is a frequentist shadow of this posterior summary. Adjoint methods (Hinze et al., 2009): PDE-constrained optimization localizes sensitivity of the objective to coefficients via adjoint states; the compiler's attribution engine is the gradient-free analogue, localizing clause failure to stages via side-effect signatures-where the forward operator is a simulator rather than a differentiable equation, signatures replace adjoints. O.6 Where the analogy ends-honestly (i) Nonstationarity: PDE coefficients do not decide to change; market operators do. The inverse solution is therefore valid only over a regime, and rolling re-certification is a structural necessity, not prudence. (ii) No ground-truth operator: unlike tomography, there is no true underlying d to recover-D is a design space, not nature's space; inverse "recovery" is inverse design. (iii) Reflexivity: widely adopted assemblies alter the forward operator itself (alpha decay as market feedback), a coupling classical inverse theory does not model; roadmap R5 names the open problem. Within these boundaries, the correspondence is exact enough to import the theory; beyond them, the framework proceeds on its own statistical feet ( §6).

p.s: O.7 Threshold calibration: the discrepancy principle
p.t: Regularization theory does not leave the regularization parameter free: the Morozov discrepancy principle (Morozov, 1966;Engl et al., 1996) chooses it so that the solution's residual matches the noise level of the data. The principle transfers directly to specification thresholds. Let δ j denote the statistical resolution of clause c j 's estimator (standard error at the evaluation horizon). Asking for margin finer than the noise floor-certifying θ j ≥ τ j with achievable margins ≪ δ j -manufactures instability: noise realizations within δ j flip the verdict (Proposition 9), and search inflates to fill the gap (Proposition 3). Asking for margin vastly coarser than δ j wastes identity the data could have certified. The discrepancy rule therefore sets thresholds where the certified assembly's margin lands at a small multiple of resolution, m j ∈ [δ j , c δ j ] with c ≈ 2-3: the strongest specification consistent with the noise floor. This upgrades the grammar's se(k) and ledger(k) floors (App. J) from discipline to principle, and it hands principals an actionable diction: do not order identity finer than your estimator can see.

p.s: O.8 A stability estimate: the condition number of a specification
p.t: Classical inverse problems report stability through a modulus of continuity (Engl et al., 1996). Here the object is elementary but informative. Perturb the specification's thresholds, τ → τ ′ = τ + ∆τ , clauses fixed. If every member of F(S) holds margin at least m min on the perturbed coordinates and |∆τ j | < m min for all j, then no member is lost: F(S) ⊆ F(S ′ ). For the reverse inclusion, a non-member e can enter only if some loosening covers its worst violation v(e) = max j (-m j (e)) + ; writing v min = min e / ∈F (S) v(e) for the distance of the closest almost-feasible assembly, |∆τ j | < min(m min , v min ) for all j gives F(S ′ ) = F (S) exactly: the feasible set is locally constant, with modulus ω(∆τ ) = 0 inside that radius. The worst margin is thus a condition number of the specification-κ(S) = 1/m min in units of estimation scale: small-margin specifications are illconditioned (threshold nudges expel shallow members or admit shallow non-members), and marginmaximizing selection ( §3.4) is conditioning improvement. Certificates that quote m min per clause therefore quote, simultaneously, the stability radius of the entire determination-one number doing the work of three.

p.s: O.9 Bayesian contraction and the effective sample size of a regime
p.t: Under the Bayesian reading of §3.4, a prior π(d) (the LLM mechanism prior) updated by T weeks of evaluation likelihood yields a posterior over satisfaction events that contracts at the parametric rate T -1/2 up to model-misspecification terms (Kaipio & Somersalo, 2005;Stuart, 2010): the certificate's confidence intervals are the frequentist shadow of this contraction. The useful refinement is what counts as T . Because the forward operator is regime-dependent, the effective sample size is the regime length, not the calendar length: a three-year window spanning four regimes certifies four T ≈ 39-week experiments, not one 156-week experiment, and contraction claims must be discounted accordingly. This quantifies the structural necessity of rolling re-certification (nonstationarity, §3.4): certificates expire because their T stops growing when the regime turns. The e-process construction of Proposition 8 is the monitoring layer that makes expiry observable rather than silent; the two theories meet exactly here-posterior contraction says how fast trust accrues within a regime, anytime validity says how to police it across regime boundaries.

p.s: P Numerical Illustration of the Inverse Problem
p.t: This appendix instantiates the inverse-problem formalism of Appendix O on the synthetic market of Section 7. Every number below is computed, not assumed; the data-generating process (DGP), seed, and code path are those of Appendix F. The purpose is not empirical validation-the market is synthetic by construction-but operational illustration: each abstract object (forward operator, feasible set, regularizer, stability estimate) is made concrete and measurable.

With |D| = 32 assemblies in the demonstration search space, the forward operator F : D × Ω → Θ is a finite map. We evaluate it at the realized market draw ω 7 (seed 7) and record, for every assembly d, the observation vector θ(d) = (IR, s style , |ρ|, s down , τ ): information ratio, style exposure, absolute correlation with the dividend-style index, downside capture, and turnover. The specification of Section 7 is Spec = {s style ≤ 6, |ρ| ≤ 0.15, s down ≥ 15%, τ ≤ 0.10}, all four clauses hard.

p.s: P.2 The feasible set is small and structured
p.t: Exactly 2 of 32 assemblies are feasible, and they are siblings: both use horizon h = 2, neutralization on, ranking on, top-N = 50, execution variant B. They differ only in the label-aggregation switch. This is a first concrete reading of Remarks 4 (existence is conditional) and 5 (non-uniqueness): the feasible set F(Spec) is neither empty nor a singleton, and its two elements share most of their genotype-feasibility is concentrated in a region of D, a fact the compiler exploits via warm-start and the analyst exploits via sensitivity reading (Section 6).

p.s: P.3 Clause margins and regularized selection
p.t: For each assembly d and clause φ j with threshold c j , define the signed margin m j (d): the distance from the observed statistic to the threshold, positive when satisfied, normalized by the clause's scale (e.g. m style = (6 -s style )/6). Let m min (d) = min j m j (d). Proposition 9 (stability through margins) is the statement that selection should trade satisfaction against margin depth, exactly as Tikhonov regularization trades data fit against solution norm. Table 23 shows the two feasible assemblies. The two feasible solutions are ordered oppositely by the two criteria: the IR-maximal feasible assembly sits barely inside the feasible region (m min = 0.073, i.e. its tightest clause is satisfied by only 7.3% of the clause scale), while the deeper-margin sibling sacrifices 1.17 IR units (17.4%) for a 67% deeper worst-case margin. This is the cost-of-specification of Proposition 2 appearing a second time, now inside the feasible set, as the price of robustness. In the inverse-problem reading: the Table 23: The feasible set at seed 7, with minimum clause margin. IR-based selection picks the first row; margin-regularized selection (Proposition 9) picks the second.
